name: Oil & Exploration
scope: Upstream oil & gas: global prices, supply and forecasts, India's output, gas pricing, levies and exploration policy, and what they mean for Indian listed producers, service and equipment firms, the gas chain and refiners.

summary.one_line: Brent is back above $105 with more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output still offline, ONGC's first Samudra Manthan deepwater well in the Mahanadi has struck gas, and a new US sanctions law on Russian oil buyers adds a fresh cost risk for Indian refiners (S2; S5; S16; S8).
key_points: Brent futures closed at $105.28/bbl on 28 September after touching $108.83, with US-Iran talks still uncertain; crude hit $113.48 on 9 September (S5; S2).
The IEA says more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output is still offline, Gulf exports are about half pre-war levels at 13 mb/d, and observed inventories have fallen 507 mb since February (S2).
Agencies disagree sharply on 2026 demand: OPEC sees +0.4 mb/d, the EIA -1.7 mb/d and the IEA -2.5 mb/d; all three see growth of 2.4-2.6 mb/d in 2027 (S3).
The EIA forecasts Brent at $91 for 2026 and $74 for 2027; banks raised forecasts in mid-September (HSBC $90 for 2026 and $85 for 2027; Goldman $85 for December 2026) (S1; S6).

ONGC struck gas on 18 September at well MN-DW18-1-H-D, 43 km off Konark - the first Mahanadi well under Samudra Manthan - with a test rate of close to 2.25 MMSCMD according to its exploration director (S16; S17).
India's crude output fell for a third straight year to 27.96 MMT in FY26; APM gas stays capped at $7.00/MMBtu while the September formula price is $9.00 (S9; S10; S11).
The US signed a law on 18 September allowing tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil; Russia supplies about 45% of India's crude imports (S8).
Welspun Corp won a record $412.5 mn US pipe order, lifting its order book to $4.7 bn; deepwater OALP-X/XI bids were pushed again to 15 November (S24; S15).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Crude producers with Brent-linked realisations: ONGC realised $99.45/bbl on nomination crude in Q1 FY27 and Oil India $98.73/bbl (S18; S19).
ONGC, if the Mahanadi find proves commercial, and Antelopus Selan, which holds 100% of the D-11 Mahanadi block with six gas discoveries (S16; S17).

Offshore service firms named as possible beneficiaries of more deepwater drilling - Jindal Drilling, Deep Industries, SEAMEC, Asian Energy - though the find is an early step, not an immediate order flow (S16; S17).
Line-pipe exporters: Welspun Corp's order book is a record $4.7 bn (S24).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Oil marketing companies while pump prices are held at ₹102.12 (petrol) and ₹95.20 (diesel) in Delhi: HPCL lost ₹12,264 cr and BPCL ₹1,873 cr in Q1 FY27 (S10; S25).
Refiners that rely on Russian barrels, now exposed to possible US tariffs under the 18 September sanctions law (S8).
LNG importers while Qatar supply is suspended: Petronet's Dahej terminal ran at 66% in Q1 FY27 against 92% a year earlier (S4).
Oil India's earnings after the June royalty reset to 16.66%; analysts cited by Business Standard estimate a 5-6% EPS hit (S13).
A US-Iran deal that reopens Hormuz: the EIA already expects Brent to fall to $74 in 2027 as Gulf output recovers (S1).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: The October APM gas price and the half-yearly deepwater/HPHT price ceiling, due around 1 October (S10; S11).
Fortnightly reviews of the export duty (SAED) on petrol, diesel and ATF (S12).
Appraisal of the Mahanadi find and Samudra Manthan implementation rules ahead of the 15 November deepwater bid deadline (S15; S17).

sections.title: The theme: a prolonged Gulf supply shock meets a falling Indian output base

blocks.text: The Gulf supply shock is in its eighth month. In its September report the IEA said more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output remains offline, August world supply fell 1.6 mb/d month on month to 100.1 mb/d, and Gulf exports were about 13 mb/d, roughly half the pre-conflict level (S2). Observed crude inventories fell 95 mb in August and 507 mb since February (S2). The IEA cut its 2026 supply estimate to 100.7 mb/d and now sees the Gulf recovery slipping into 2027, when supply rebounds by 8 mb/d (S2).

Prices have climbed back. The EIA puts August's Brent average at $91, $7 above July (S1). Crude hit $113.48 on 9 September (S2), and Brent futures closed at $105.28 on 28 September after trading as high as $108.83 amid uncertainty over US-Iran talks (S5). OPEC+ left October output policy unchanged at its 6 September meeting and must agree new 2027 baselines before further unwinding cuts (S7).

blocks.text: The agencies differ on demand, not on direction: the IEA expects demand to shrink 2.5 mb/d in 2026 because of product disruptions and high fuel prices, while OPEC still sees growth (S2; S3). For 2027 the EIA and IEA both expect supply growth to outpace demand as Gulf output returns, which is why the EIA sees Brent falling to $74 (S1; S2; S3).

subsections.title: India: shrinking output, heavy import dependence

blocks.text: India's crude output fell for a third straight year to 27.96 MMT in FY26, down about 3%, which the government blames on natural decline in ageing fields; ONGC held its own decline to about 2% through enhanced and improved oil recovery (S9). India imports about 88-90% of its crude (S9; S15) and about half its gas (S16).

Sourcing is the new pressure point. Russia supplies about 45% of India's crude imports; India took about 2.08 mb/d from Russia in August, down from 2.82 mb/d (56% of imports) in July (S8). On 18 September the US signed a law letting the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, reviewed every 180 days; it does not impose tariffs on India automatically (S8).
Retail prices remain held: petrol was ₹102.12/litre and diesel ₹95.20/litre in Delhi on 28 September (S10). Higher crude therefore shows up in refiners' losses rather than at the pump (S25).

blocks.text: Windfall tax on domestic crude: the September duty revision covers petrol, diesel and ATF exports only and gives no rate for domestically produced crude (S12). ONGC's Q1 FY27 realisation of $99.45/bbl is consistent with no large crude levy in that quarter (S18). We could not confirm a current domestic-crude levy from a primary source.

subsections.title: Exploration policy and the first Samudra Manthan result

blocks.caption: Samudra Manthan (National Offshore Exploration Scheme)
rows: 60 wells; government pays up to 50% of eligible cost or ₹675 cr per well, whichever is lower (S14)
Modern offshore seismic acquisition and processing (S14)
Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zones
Local manufacturing of equipment and services (S14)
Up to FY2030-31; targets reserve accretion of over 600 MMTOE (S14)

items: ONGC struck gas on 18 September at MN-DW18-1-H-D, drilled to 1,623 m with gas at 1,441-1,452 m, about 43 km off Konark; it is the first Mahanadi well of the Samudra Manthan campaign (S17).

ONGC's exploration director said the well tested close to 2.25 MMSCMD (S16). Next steps are flow-rate results, more drilling and confirmation of commercial reserves, so it is an early step rather than an immediate production boost (S17).
Deepwater wells cost about $125-150 mn each, which is why the 50% cost support matters (S9).

Bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks in OALP-X (25 blocks, 13 deep/ultra-deep) and OALP-XI (21 blocks, 5 deep/ultra-deep) were extended again to 15 November 2026, pending the scheme's implementation rules (S15).
The repeated extensions show the difficulty of attracting investors to technically demanding offshore acreage (S15).

Oil India plans to drill 100 wells in FY27, commission its Numaligarh coker unit in Q3 FY27 and the rest of the expansion by March 2027, and drill a fourth Andaman well in December 2026 (S19). It guides to 3.9-4.0 MMT of crude in FY27 (S20).
Vedanta Oil & Gas's output fell to 87,200 boepd in FY26 from 103,200; ICRA expects enhanced oil recovery and infill drilling in Rajasthan to partly offset decline, with calibrated capex (S21).
Deep Industries guides FY27 capex of ₹250-300 cr, tied to contract wins, and expects its ₹1,402 cr, 15-year ONGC production-enhancement contract to start contributing from October 2026 (S22).
Maharashtra Seamless has ₹714 cr of ONGC and Oil India orders, 42% of its ₹1,709 cr order book (S23).

blocks.text: In mid-September Goldman Sachs, HSBC, Bank of America and Commerzbank all raised Brent forecasts because Gulf disruption is lasting longer; their near-term calls range from $83 (BofA, 2H26) to $90 (HSBC, 2026) (S6). Goldman and BofA both flag $120 upside risk (S6).

items: Peace risk for producers: a reopened Hormuz would release Gulf supply; the EIA expects Brent to fall to $74 in 2027 as output recovers (S1; S2).
Escalation risk for refiners and gas users: BofA sees $150 if energy infrastructure is badly damaged (S6).
US tariffs on Russian oil buyers could force costlier crude sourcing (S8).
Policy flip-flops: the onshore royalty cut in May was reversed in June (S13).
Exploration risk: the Mahanadi find still needs appraisal, and deepwater bid rounds keep slipping (S15; S17).

companies.name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation
companies.role: India's largest crude and gas producer; Q1 FY27 output 4.452 MMT crude and 4.756 BCM gas (S18).
companies.impact: Brent-linked crude ($99.45/bbl in Q1) and $13.31 new-well gas more than doubled standalone PAT; the Mahanadi deepwater find (about 2.25 MMSCMD tested) adds exploration upside, but APM gas is capped at $7 (S11; S16; S18).

companies.name: Oil India
companies.role: State E&P focused on onshore fields and frontier basins, owning the Numaligarh refinery (S19).
companies.impact: Most leveraged to crude volume growth (+11% in Q1) and NRL margins, but the June royalty reset cuts EPS by an estimated 5-6% (S13; S19).

companies.name: Vedanta Oil & Gas
companies.role: Private E&P anchored by the Rajasthan block, with Ravva and Cambay; 87,200 boepd in FY26 (S21).
companies.impact: Low cost ($15-16/boe) gives strong margins at $100 oil, but output is declining and the Rajasthan PSC expires in May 2030 (S21).

companies.name: Antelopus Selan Energy
companies.role: Small E&P holding 100% of the D-11 Mahanadi offshore block with six gas discoveries (S16).
companies.impact: Direct geological read-across from ONGC's Mahanadi find, though the find itself is early-stage (S16; S17).

companies.name: Hindustan Oil Exploration Company
companies.role: Small E&P with offshore exploration and production assets (S16).
companies.impact: Gains from high crude and offshore-exploration sentiment; no direct link to the Mahanadi well (S16; S17).

companies.name: Jindal Drilling & Industries
companies.impact: Holds a three-year ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer; more offshore drilling could lift rig demand over time (S16; S17).

companies.name: Deep Industries
companies.role: Oilfield services: gas compression, drilling and production enhancement (S22).
companies.impact: Order book ₹3,047 cr and a ₹1,402 cr ONGC production-enhancement contract expected to contribute from October 2026 (S22).

companies.name: SEAMEC
companies.role: Diving, inspection and offshore maintenance services (S16).
companies.impact: Named among likely beneficiaries of more offshore activity after the Mahanadi find (S16).

companies.name: Asian Energy Services
companies.impact: Named as a possible beneficiary of expanded exploration activity (S16).

companies.name: Maharashtra Seamless
companies.role: Seamless pipe and OCTG maker with ₹714 cr of ONGC and Oil India orders (S23).
companies.impact: Tubular demand tracks well counts such as Oil India's 100-well FY27 plan; anti-dumping duty expiry in January 2027 is a risk (S19; S23).

companies.name: Welspun Corp
companies.role: Line-pipe maker with a US subsidiary, Welspun Tubular LLC (S24).
companies.impact: A record $412.5 mn US HFIW order lifts the global order book to $4.7 bn, executed in FY28-29 (S24).

method: Week-40 refresh of the 2026-W38 edition, researched on 29 September 2026 with web search and page fetches. We re-verified carried-over facts (EIA September STEO read directly from the PDF; IEA September report via World Oil; ICRA's Vedanta Oil & Gas rationale read from the PDF; ONGC, Oil India, Petronet, Deep Industries and Maharashtra Seamless Q1 FY27 figures re-opened) and added this week's changes: Brent's move above $105, mid-September bank forecast upgrades, the IEF comparison of agency demand forecasts, ONGC's Mahanadi gas discovery, the US Russia-sanctions law, the 16 September export-duty revision, the OALP deadline extension and Welspun's new order. Some facts come from search-result snippets of pages that blocked direct fetching (CNBC, Business Standard, Upstox article-200612, PPAC pages); the Outlook India and OilPrice dates are approximate to the publication week/month. Items from last week that we could not re-confirm today were dropped rather than carried forward - including the PPAC Ready Reckoner import-bill series, OPEC spare-capacity estimates, older bank forecasts (Citi, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan), IOC, GAIL, city gas and small-cap service results, Reliance KG-D6 data and L&T/EIL/MAN/Jindal Saw orders. IGL's Q1 profit was reported differently by sources (₹186 cr standalone, -48%, versus ₹237.9 cr consolidated, -44%), so we left IGL out this week. Market-cap coverage runs from large caps (ONGC, BPCL, HPCL) through mid caps (Oil India, Petronet, Welspun, Vedanta Oil & Gas) to small caps (Antelopus Selan, HOEC, Jindal Drilling, Deep Industries, SEAMEC, Asian Energy, Maharashtra Seamless). No ratings or price targets are ours; broker targets are quoted as published.
